data.why: A gas tank water heater stands cut open in a laundry room with a person waiting at its hot tap; the water and the heat are followed from the flame under the tank, round the jacket, up the flue, in through the dip tube and out the hot tap. The camera opens close on the burner and the tank, frames each added part, and ends on hot water pouring from the tap.

recurring.what: a person waiting at the hot tap

chain.shows: heat leaks out through the thin walls and the water cools

the flame relights and its fumes spill into the laundry room

surprises.claim: The U.S. Department of Energy recommends setting a water heater's thermostat to 120 degrees Fahrenheit.
surprises.search: Department of Energy water heater thermostat 120 degrees Fahrenheit

surprises.claim: A tank water heater's dip tube carries incoming cold water to the bottom of the tank so it does not mix with the hot water at the top.
surprises.search: water heater dip tube cold water bottom of tank

surprises.claim: A water heater's anode rod, usually magnesium or aluminum, corrodes instead of the steel tank.
surprises.search: water heater anode rod magnesium sacrificial corrodes instead of tank

sentences.text: If you light a flame under a tank, you have a water heater.
But heat leaks out, and the water cools.
So you wrap the tank in foam.
But the foam keeps the water heating past scalding.
So a thermostat shuts the flame off at 120 degrees.
But the flame's fumes spill out under the tank.
So a flue carries the hot fumes outside.
But at the hot tap, cold refill water mixes in.
So a dip tube sends the cold water to the bottom.
But that fresh water slowly rusts the steel tank.
So a magnesium rod rusts away instead of the tank.
Open the tap, and hot water pours out.
Congratulations, you built a water heater.
